chunks: 1976 - Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله called a group who fasted when he broke the fast and shortened the prayer, the disobedient."
He said: "And they are the disobedient until the Day of Judgment, and we indeed recognize their sons and the sons of their sons up to this day of ours."

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, the Imam reporting the teaching
key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: he broke the fast, referring to the Prophetic practice during travel
key_terms.الْعُصَاةَ: the disobedient, the description given to those who opposed this ruling
key_terms.حَرِيزٌ: Hariz, a narrator in the sanad
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurarah, a narrator transmitting from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام
key_terms.صَامُوا: they fasted, referring to maintaining the fast during travel
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: he shortened, referring to shortening the prayer in travel
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, indicating the enduring nature of this designation

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about fasting during travel when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله broke his fast and shortened the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states that those who continued fasting during travel when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had broken the fast and shortened the prayer were designated as disobedient. It emphasizes the binding authority of the Prophetic sunnah in travel-related rulings and presents this opposition as an enduring pattern.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1976 - Hariz narrated from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:
"The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) called a group of people who fasted when he broke his fast and shortened his prayer as 'disobedient.'
He (sw) said: 'They are disobedient until the Day of Judgment, and we recognize their children and the children of their children up to this day of ours.'"
